result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use a boolean formal conditionExpression on a conditional flow only when the description supports the condition.
Give the outgoing sequence flows of an event-based gateway no conditionExpression; the first occurring target event selects the path.
Use a complex gateway only for an explicitly described rule that XOR, OR and AND cannot express. Prefer separate split and join gateways for clarity.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.

result.rule: When the description states a yes/no decision by an actor that determines whether the process continues, and it names a distinct outcome for the negative case (the process ends without a result): Model an exclusive gateway at the point where the decision is made. Give one outgoing branch a condition for the continuing case, which leads to the next activity, and give the other branch a condition for the negative case, which leads to its own end event labelled for that outcome. Do not merge the negative outcome into the main end event, and do not leave the decision as a plain sequence with no gateway.

When the description says that a later step is reached only after the other party approves an earlier deliverable, and then names a separate follow-up action that occurs after that approval and before a step that records the outcome in a system: Model the separately named follow-up action as its own task. Place it after the approval decision and before the recording task, with the flow running approval, then the follow-up task, then recording. Do not fold it into the recording task or drop it, even when the description presents the approval and the recording as one continuous sequence.
